title: JSON WEB TOKENS
summaryPoints: HTTP is stateless; a JWT lets the client carry its identity with every request.
A JWT is a header, a payload of claims and a signature, joined by dots.
The parts are Base64URL: encoded, not encrypted, so anyone can read them.
Encoding changes format, signing proves integrity and origin, encryption hides content.
HS256 signs with a shared secret; RS256 and ES256 use a key pair published as JWKS.
Always verify the signature and the claims exp, nbf, iss and aud, and pin the algorithm.
Keep access tokens short-lived and never put secrets in the payload.

chapters.name: INTRO
chapters.summary: You log in once but make hundreds of requests; a JWT is how the server keeps recognising you.

chapters.name: WHY TOKENS
chapters.summary: Sessions store state on the server; a token carries it with the request, and any server with the key can check it.

chapters.name: ANATOMY
chapters.summary: A JWT is a header, a payload of claims and a signature, joined by dots.

chapters.name: BASE64URL
chapters.summary: Base64URL turns bytes into URL-safe text; it is encoding, so anyone can reverse it.

chapters.name: ENCODE SIGN ENCRYPT
chapters.summary: Encoding changes format, signing proves integrity and origin, encryption hides content; a normal JWT is encoded and signed only.

chapters.name: SIGNING
chapters.summary: HS256 signs header and payload with a shared secret; the server recomputes to verify and rejects any tampering.

chapters.name: KEYS
chapters.summary: A shared secret lets every verifier sign too; a key pair lets only the auth server sign, and JWKS publishes the public keys.

chapters.name: CLAIMS
chapters.summary: A valid signature is not enough: the server checks exp, nbf, iss and aud, and short lifetimes limit damage.

chapters.name: IN PRACTICE
chapters.summary: The login-to-API flow with a Bearer header, where to store the token, and how Quarkus verifies it.

chapters.name: PITFALLS
chapters.summary: alg none, algorithm confusion, weak secrets, secrets in the payload and missing revocation.

chapters.name: RECAP
chapters.summary: A JWT is signed, not secret: verify the signature and the claims, pin the algorithm, keep tokens short.
